report.summary: Reviewed the Cycle26 PLAN ONLY packet (source-business-evidence.ts, exact-copy-evidence.ts, assessment-evidence-scope.ts, delivery-assessment.ts, contracts.ts, skill) against the proposed deep pure module positive-literal-source-witness.ts. The integration shape is sound (raw status supported + business all-unknown-dynamic + witness covered -> skip only the business gate), but the typed-plan parsing and unit/owner-witness rules leave concrete unsafe acceptance paths. The biggest are: (1) the directive grammar does not pin the literal's position, so trailing operational language (e.g. '… include the literal phrase "Updated daily" at runtime') is silently allowed; (2) the parser does not reject stacked/contrastive negations or modifiers attached to the literal; (3) 'literal unique in safe source text' plus 'exact model citations cover complete owner' admit a model-emitted duplicate duplicate witness gap via incomplete citation excerpt slices (the witness checks coverage of the expected owner, not that the model quote belongs to a text-only owner, and after replacing the explanation the model excerpt is never re-validated); (4) plan says 'reject ambiguous directive tails' but defines no tail vocabulary, so 'in one p tag', '(case-insensitive)', 'anywhere', 'once' tails can alter semantics or make coverage impossible while still being accepted as the exact typed plan; (5) planned status/ledger wording is not anchored to a concrete predicate, risking accidental 'unchanged'/prior-failure rewrites in the quarantine ledger and old-15 replay. All findings are plan-level (planned absent file vs logic bug vs missing narrow condition are labelled in each title). No runtime, tests, or replay were executed; all checks are unexecuted reasoning traces over the supplied code.

findings.title: PLAN GAP (missing narrow condition): typed coverage-2 plan can be admitted as source_text/literal_content while its directive grammar carries an operation clause, because sourceOnlyDirective short-circuits the OBSERVATION_REQUIRED veto for target criteria
findings.evidence: delivery-assessment.ts:278 calls assessmentEvidenceScope(criterion). assessment-evidence-scope.ts:162 sets sourceOnlyDirective=true when exactCopyLiteral(criterion.source) is defined. Lines 166–175: for sourceOnlyDirective the only veto is OBSERVATION_REQUIRED.test(title) (title only; the source clause is never tested) plus the relation/visibility title test. A source such as 'The menu.html page copy must include the literal phrase "Updated daily" at runtime/dynamically/automatically every day' therefore classifies as {category:'source_text', reason:'literal_content'} provided the title does not contain a veto token. The proposed plan ('Finite full-source English grammar only The <explicit.html path|full menu> page copy must include the literal phrase <one bounded literal>', 'Reject negation/condition/compound/multiple sentences and ambiguous directive tails') depends on the SAME exactCopyLiteral path being able to reject the trailing tail, but the plan gives that parser no explicit tail grammar and no explicit list of rejected suffix vocabularies. If the new witness module's parser is the only thing enforcing the tail and the existing scope classifier is left as-is (line 162 unchanged), a plan accepted by the new parser can still be admitted with an operation tail the buyer never agreed to check (runtime update, live data, per-load). This is a safety hole, not a missing file: the proposed module does not state that it must either (a) reject the tail (preventing the source_text/business validation downstream of it) or (b) coordinate with assessmentEvidenceScope so the same tail is refused at scope classification.
findings.reproduction: UNEXECUTED reasoning trace: criterion = {id:'coverage-2', title:'Menu copy', source:'The menu.html page copy must include the literal phrase "Updated daily" at runtime.'}. exactCopyLiteral(...) returns true if it accepts the literal before the trailing text; assessmentEvidenceScope returns source_text/literal_content (line 172 tests withoutWorkingTimeUnits(title) only). positive-literal-source-witness.ts accepts because the literal is grounded and source-located; delivery-assessment.ts:342 sees kind 'unknown' with all unknown reasons dynamic_or_unsupported_source, witness covered -> new branch keeps supported. Model reply 'supported' survives, now claiming runtime-updated text as a source-only match. No browser/runtime evidence was used, and the explanation is required to say 'no visible/actually updated/runtime proof', so the status contradicts the operation language the buyer actually wrote.
findings.suggestion: State explicitly, in the plan, that the new module exposes the directive-tail decision and that delivery-assessment.ts:342 only runs when that same decision is 'exact typed plan' with zero tail (or that assessmentEvidenceScope line 162 must not treat a directive with a non-whitespace tail as literal). Minimal fix: define the literal tail as exactly end-of-source (optionally a period/quote/whitespace) and refuse every other suffix; and note the requirement that the witness module's acceptance predicate is the only gate for 'the typed plan is the source-text scope', so it cannot diverge from assessmentEvidenceScope.

The package states that the CURRENT gate is unknown due to importmap/module JS and missing Bootstrap CSS; that is exactly the file-level case. The plan says 'all linked business unknown checks are only dynamic_or_unsupported_source and positive witness covered' then skip the business gate. 'Linked business unknown checks' here are the SAME file-level unknown reasons regardless of whether the criterion is a pure typed coverage-2 directive or a compound criterion like 'menu must include the phrase and prices must be updated daily'. The exact-copy check at delivery-assessment.ts:381–386 rescues 'unknown' for exact-copy directives by changing to insufficient_evidence, but a compound directive that also happens to pass exactCopyLiteral can flip from insufficient_evidence to supported under the new bypass. The plan contains no statement that the criterion.source must be EXACTLY the typed grammar (not just 'contains a literal'); the task's own text says 'Exact typed plan all this criterion checks visible_copy', i.e. the plan intends this, but as a plan it does not say the implementation must verify source === typed-plan reconstruction, not merely that a literal can be extracted.

findings.title: PLAN GAP (missing narrow condition): model citation covered-by-excerpt-span check does not constrain the model excerpt to be a safe source-located text owner, so a model excerpt from an aria-hidden/hidden/inert template duplicate can satisfy 'exact model citations cover complete owner'
findings.evidence: delivery-assessment.ts:363–379: for catalog_slots, supported is gated on presenceCheck where the model citation must cover the server-returned presence citation; the catalog resolver (assessment-citation-catalog.ts, not in packet) presumably restricts catalog spans to displayed text segments. But the plan's NEW deep witness tests citations by array membership/spans against expected. The plan's phrase 'exact model citations cover complete owner' does not state that the model's citation must be an owner accepted by the SAME safe-owner rules (text-only p/li, no hidden/inert/aria-hidden ancestors, no template/foreign, no dynamic attrs). Without that, the witness can be satisfied by a model citation that covers the expected span start/end while the citation itself is, e.g., a wider div span including a hidden duplicate; the plan's rule about duplicates ('duplicate target text/owners') would then not fire if the second occurrence is in a different AST context that the module classifies as inert but the citation spans avoid. findings.title: PLAN RISK: source_presence/universal checks are skipped in the ordering for the new branch; the plan's integration condition says 'skip only old business unknown gate, not mismatch/otherchecks/otherlaterguards', but delivery-assessment.ts:363–418 run after the business block and the plan does not name the exact insertion point that preserves them (risk of accidental total short-circuit if the new witness is placed at line 342–361 without re-entering the exact-copy/label/tag/list guards)
findings.evidence: delivery-assessment.ts lines 342–362 contain the supported business block; lines 363–418 contain catalog presence, exact-copy (line 380–387), label citation, universal tag and list guards, then line 419 no-citations. If the new branch sets status via a direct assignment to 'supported' and bypasses the else-chain (e.g., early continue or an if/else where the new path replaces the business block body with a terminal assignment), subsequent guards would not run. The plan text says 'skip only old business unknown gate, not mismatch/otherchecks/otherlaterguards', which is the correct intent, but the delivery-assessment.ts structure makes the safe implementation non-obvious: the business block currently lives inside the status==='supported' branch inside the else of requires_observation, and the later guards are all after it. A minimal-safe design is to leave the code path intact and only change the businessEvidenceCheck result interpretation; the plan does not state that the business check must still be computed and only the unknown reason enumerated.
findings.reproduction: UNEXECUTED: if the implementer inserts an early return/continue after a successful new witness to avoid the business gate (a natural reading of 'skip the old gate'), exactCopyCheck at line 381 and labelCitationCheck at line 389 no longer run. A model could then claim supported for a criterion where the exact literal is missing from safe text (e.g., punctuation differs) and the witness module (which only covers positive literal) would still pass if the model cites the expected owner. This is the kind of unguarded path the plan must forbid explicitly.
findings.suggestion: Plan should say: the business gate is replaced in-place by a predicate on the businessEvidenceCheck result (if any unknown reason != dynamic_or_unsupported_source -> keep unknown; if any mismatch -> keep mismatch; if all unknown == dynamic_or_unsupported_source AND the typed plan is exact AND witness covered -> fall through), and no earlier-guard / later-guard block is moved or short-circuited; the new module is called IN the existing supported branch to decide only the business-unknown disposition.

findings.title: PLAN MISSING CONDITION: witness reason union has 'covered'|'unknown' with 'literal_source_present' but the new typed plan needs an explicit negative statuses (not_applicable|unwitnessed|covered) and a reason for 'not this exact typed criterion' so the new branch cannot be invoked for partial matches
findings.evidence: source-business-evidence.ts:10–13 defines SourceBusinessCitationWitness reason values; the plan proposes a NEW module with interface factory(files,savedBusinessSteps)(criterion,exactCitations) -> not_applicable|unwitnessed|covered. The plan does not say what not_applicable covers (no linked check vs. criterion not typed plan) and what 'unwitnessed' means when the criterion IS typed but the safe text search fails versus when all business checks are not all dynamic_or_unsupported_source. If not_applicable collapses 'no linked checks' with 'criterion is not the exact typed grammar', the new bypass could be applied to a criterion with a dynamic tail that the typed grammar rejected (since literal exists elsewhere) — see P1 #1. The new interface should distinguish 'not the exact typed plan' from 'no business checks'.
findings.reproduction: UNEXECUTED: criterion 'coverage-2' becomes a template with prices and an exact literal. If the exact-copy path changes the criterion's source before calling positive-literal-source-witness (from an upstream normalization) and the source matches the typed grammar text but not the saved visible_copy text, not_applicable would silently fall through to the old business unknown gate (safe but slower) OR be misused as 'covered' if the implementation conflates the two. The plan's phrase 'dedup identical viewport repetitions only' and 'exact typed plan' imply the exact identity must be passed as criterion, which the interface does do, but no explicit 'literal === saved expected text' precondition is stated.
findings.suggestion: Define the new module's return type explicitly with distinct reasons: {kind:'not_typed_plan'} vs {kind:'no_linked_business_check'} as not_applicable; unwitnessed reasons including 'literal_missing_or_not_unique','non_safe_owner','model_span_not_exact_slice','business_check_not_dynamic_only'; and covered only when business check expected.text === typed literal && expected.kind==='visible_copy' && check reason 'literal_source_present'. State in the plan that delivery-assessment.ts must call the module only inside the existing supported branch, not before scope classification.
